name: Contextual dominant primary action
summary: For a single closely related decision group, system-specific guidance favors one visually dominant main action with subordinate alternatives.
problem: Multiple equally dominant controls may make the next step unclear in a bounded decision context.
context: Single-step service pages or one related group of actions with a discernible main task.
observed_solution: Use the system's prominent primary/default style for its main action and less-prominent variants for secondary actions.
rationale: Both GOV.UK and Primer independently describe a limited high-priority main control and secondary/default alternatives (W02-O08, W02-O12).
tradeoffs: May obscure equally important alternatives if tasks genuinely have equal priority.
Splitting independent action groups can be more appropriate than flattening a whole page to one primary control.
applicability: One workflow decision group with one clearly preferred progression.
non_applicability: Multiple distinct sections with independent primary actions.
Scenarios with equally valid, explicit alternatives requiring balanced presentation.
accessibility_implications: Visual hierarchy does not replace accessible name, role, keyboard or focus requirements (W02-O01–O05).
responsive_implications: No measured responsive-layout result; grouping needs separate viewport evaluation.
implementation_notes: Map native action/navigation semantics separately from visual variant.
Do not prescribe exact button color or a universal page-level numerical cap.

counterexamples.summary: Independent regions may each have a primary action without being mutually competing.
counterexamples.context: Different panels with distinct task scopes.

version_context: GOV.UK and Primer live design-system guidance retrieved 2026-10-08, unpinned versions
